title: What blocks the dispatcher's event loop for 2.3 s again and again while chunk mappings and a draft run
runtime: none: no Docker, no provider or model call. Benchmark E:/ulpin-tmp/s9-6s/bench.mts, output bench-out.json.
inputs: Synthetic test_only tables (4, 7 and 15 columns; 16-row chunks; 2000 rows) and a synthetic 12-sheet draft.

chunkMappingRun.sync: zod parse; one SELECT. Learner path only, no file read.

chunkMappingRun.step: raw rows zod parse and header fingerprint per row

chunkMappingRun.step: learnerVersion: readFileSync manifest.json (twice per routed layout)
lookupMappingMemory: readFileSync + JSON.parse + zod of accepted-plans.jsonl
chunkMappingRun.drivenBy: accepted-plans.jsonl lines (runtime size unknown; not measured)

step: STUDENT: spawnSync python -m geo.usp_learning.stage_a predict (numpy + sklearn import, np.load
at: U/chunk-mapping-agent.ts:167,211 (routeLayout, only when the job-local layout cache misses)

validateMappingPlanV2 (x2-3), executeTeacherMappingDryRun, verifiedProposal, questions, metrics zod

machine: this PC (Windows 11, Node 24.19.0, venv-k3a-geo Python, learner E:/BhuAayam-data/task-data/a4/learner/v43)

15columnsWithStudent.laterChunks: wall < 5 ms; block reads 10.6-15.4 = Windows timer granularity

name: Synchronous local student prediction: callStudent runs spawnSync python stage_a predict
cost: 2.6 s on this PC (2.59 s of it is importing numpy and sklearn; bare Python start is 66 ms; the model, rows
and column count barely matter). Run 7 measured 2.2-2.4 s.
active: Rehearsal and demo runtimes require the intact v43 seed and a Windows python.exe
(scripts/platform/demo-config.mjs:167-206), so learnerVersion is non-null and the student runs.
whyItRepeats: Every table gets its own proposal_only chunk-mapping job with a new TabularChunkMapper
(U/chunk-mapping-worker.ts:515), so its first chunk misses the job-local layout cache and routes the
layout: one blocking Python start per table.
The kit has 3 CSVs and a 12-sheet workbook: 15 tables. Run 7 logged exactly 15 stalls of 2.2-2.4 s after
the 8.4 s one: 3 at 21-44 s (the CSVs), and 12 at 624-676 s, right after the workbook draft finished
The 12 come in pairs about 0.7 s apart, then about 4 s to the next pair: two chunk-mapping jobs at a time
(holding chunk-mapping x2), each blocking 2.3 s in turn. The timing is consistent with two lanes; the lane
cap and dispatch tick were not re-measured here.
intake-draft and streaming-vector are held but are not the cause: the workbook draft job waits for upload
slots for minutes, and its only synchronous work measured 0.2 ms per draft fingerprint.
notExplained: The 8.4 s stall at 8.5 s held seven jobs; one student call can be up to 2.6 s of it. The rest is not
relatedSameKind: trainOfficerBatch spawnSync python stage_a train (U/chunk-mapping-learning.ts:100) blocks the loop the same
way when an approved table recipe teaches the learner; not on the run 7 path (no approval).

why: The fix stores, matches and decides nothing differently, but it is not a one-function change: callStudent,
remainingStudent and proposeMapping all become async, and the spawnSync mocks in
mapping-rules.test.ts:77-115 and tests/tabular-admission.test.ts:352 must move to spawn. The new process
code (stdin EPIPE, timeout kill, maxBuffer) also needs the full server suite. That is more than DO 4 allows
in this time box, so it stays a proposal.

change: In mapping-teacher.ts make callStudent async: spawn the same command, args, env, 30000 ms timeout and 1
MiB stdout cap; write JSON.stringify(inputs) to stdin and handle stdin 'error' (EPIPE) so it cannot crash
the process; resolve on close; any error, non-zero exit, timeout or overflow returns STUDENT_UNAVAILABLE
as now; parse and check exactly as now. Await it in remainingStudent and at mapping-teacher.ts:941.
sameOutputs: Same inputs, same Python, same parsing and the same fallback code, so the fields, codes and plans are
identical. Test: on generated profiles (4/7/15 columns), the old spawnSync path and the new async path
return deepEqual results, with a 5 ms timer firing during the call (skip when ULPIN_PROFILE_PYTHON or the
seed is absent); move the two spawnSync mocks to spawn.
risk: Low to moderate. No stored, matched or decided change. Two chunk-mapping jobs can now run Python at once
(about 2.6 s CPU and one sklearn process each) instead of one after another. A fence can now lapse during
the call, as it already can for teacher calls; publishing still asserts the attempt.
biggerAlternative: A long-lived predictor process (one import, many predictions) cuts each call from 2.6 s to milliseconds,
but it needs a new process lifecycle: not proposed for the freeze.
proposal.notEnough: Caching predictions by layout would not help: every kit table has its own layout.
